survey: A spiral topiary of four stacked foliage tiers that shrink toward the top. It sits in brown soil inside a round, low stone planter. The planter rests on a pink flagstone path that curves away to the right, with a lawn and a tall clipped hedge behind it. The camera is a little above the planter. The horizon is at about the base of the hedge, so the planter's rim and soil show as a fairly open ellipse. The stone blocks along the rim curve and shorten as they wrap around the ellipse. The lower tiers sit below eye level, so their joins bow slightly downward. The upper tiers reach toward eye level and look nearly side-on, which fits the low camera. The topiary rises straight up from the centre of the soil. The flagstones get smaller toward the back, and the path's curved edge recedes to the same horizon as the lawn and hedge. The planter sits flat on the paving, at the angle the ground is drawn.
